followUps: How does 'My mercy encompasses all things' fit with eternal punishment, and with the second half of 7:156 that limits it to 'those who fear Me'?
Was the Prophet (pbuh) merciful to his enemies too? What examples show it?
doubter.why: Warm and well sourced, but 7:156 is quoted in full, including 'My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will', and the obvious tension is never addressed.

followUps: What do 'iḥsān', 'Ar-Rahman' and 'zakah' mean, and why is iḥsān in the title but only defined in a one-line answer at the end?
How does this mercy fit with harsh punishments and war in Islamic law?
outsider.why: The animal and child stories make mercy vivid, but iḥsān, half the title, gets one line, and the harder side of the tradition is not mentioned.

followUps: Where are the scholars? What did al-Ghazali, Ibn al-Qayyim or others say about rahma and iḥsān, and what is the full Hadith Jibril definition of iḥsān?
How do the fuqaha apply Muslim 1955 (iḥsān in slaughter) in the schools' rules of dhabh?
student.why: Eight graded hadith and Ibn Kathir with Qatada and al-Hasan al-Basri are strong evidence, but there is no scholars section at all and iḥsān is barely developed.

followUps: Is there research on compassion or kindness (e.g. compassion training, prosocial behaviour) that relates to this teaching?
Is 'mercy is learned' a claim about psychology, and if so what supports it?
scientist.why: Nothing scientific is overclaimed, but nothing scientific is offered either, and 'Mercy is learned' sounds like a behavioural claim without support.

followUps: I was raised with harshness; how exactly do I start practising a softer heart?
If I have been harsh to my own children, is there mercy for me?
hurting.why: 'If you were raised with harshness, you can still ask for, and practise, a softer heart' is gentle and hopeful, but the section is two sentences.

followUps: Why quote 7:156 in full and skip the tension between universal mercy and limited, severe punishment?
The page infers 'Mercy is learned' from 3:159, which says the gentleness was 'by mercy from Allah' (a gift); isn't that a stretch?
skeptic.why: The selection is entirely positive, and the only critique admitted is about Muslims' behaviour, not about the texts on punishment.

missing: Address the tension in 7:156 between 'mercy encompasses all things' and punishment / the limiting clause
Develop iḥsān (it is in the title): Hadith Jibril definition and what it asks in practice
Add a scholars section with named works
Give concrete steps for the hurting reader and for parents
strengths: Rich, well-graded hadith set (mercy in a hundred parts, the dog, kissing al-Hasan)
3:159 read carefully: mercy paired with pardon, prayer and consultation
'Does mercy mean never being firm?' answered well
